messages.author: 08525297474c6938
messages.subject: Error plotting using RApache
parts:
Hi,

I get "Error in plot.new() : could not open file '/var/www/
sample.png'\n" in the apache error log when I tried the following
configuration on my local machine.

// httpd.conf

LoadModule R_module /usr/lib/apache2/modules/mod_R.so

<VirtualHost *:80>
ServerAdmin root@localhost
DocumentRoot /var/www/
</VirtualHost>

<Location /RApacheInfo>
SetHandler r-info
</Location>

<Location /rapachetest>
SetHandler r-handler
RFileHandler /var/www/test.R::hello
</Location>

-------------------------------------------------------------

// test.R code

hello<-function(){
setContentType("text/html")
png(file="/var/www/sample.png")

x <- c(1,3,6,9,12)
y <- c(1.5,2,7,8,15)
plot(x,y)
dev.off()

cat("<html>")
cat("<body>")
cat("<h1>hello world</h1>")
cat("</body>")
cat("</html>")
OK
}

Could someone guide me on how I could I go about solving the problem ?

Thanks in advance.
Rohit

messages.author: fe0b9140b8bdf3c1
messages.subject: Re: Error plotting using RApache
parts:
Hi Rohit -

A few thoughts/things to try:

1. Use the print() command to explicitly render plots to disk inside
non-interactive sessions. This particular one has bitten me before.
E.g.

p <- plot(x,y)
print(p)
dev.off()

2. Run your script outside of Apache session, running under Apache's
userid (usually 'www-data' or 'httpd'), and see if it works.
(Stripping out the RApache specific commands like 'setContentType')

sudo -u www-data R --vanilla hello.R

Check the file to see if it properly wrote out the png to /var/www?
If you point your browser to this location do you see it?


3. It's probably worth noting that the code you provided, even if it
ran, would not render an image to the browser. You would need to
include an "img src" tag that points to the image you created.

It does two separate things:

(i) it creates a plot and writes it to disk
(ii) it then cats "hello world" to the browser

I'll send a working "helloworld.R" script that you can crib in a
separate e-mail.

After doing chmod 777 to the /var/www folder it worked.

Thanks,
Rohit
